summary: First backend testing pass for 'What's In My Wardrobe' API. 40/40 pytest tests passed (100%) covering auth (register/login/me/profile, JWT validation), AI tag-item with real Pexels fashion image (GPT-5.2 via emergentintegrations), Items CRUD with filters (category/color/favorite), auth scoping between two users, AI stylist (returned valid item_ids from user's catalog only), Outfits CRUD + favorite toggle, Lookbooks (list/detail/recreate, including empty closet branch), and camera-roll scan (2 images → 2 items added). One transient 500 was observed on first run for /api/lookbooks/{id}/recreate due to Emergent LLM key budget cap ('Current cost: 0.00613725, Max budget: 0.001'), which cleared on rerun.

minor.issue: Both endpoints raise HTTPException(500) on any LlmChat failure (including transient budget/rate-limit errors from the Emergent LLM gateway). Recommend graceful fallback consistent with the empty-closet branch: return 200 with {message: 'Couldn\'t generate looks right now, try again.', outfit/outfits: null/[]} so the mobile client doesn't surface a hard error toast for a recoverable LLM hiccup.

EmailStr validation rejects .test TLD (emails ending in @something.test return 422). Not a real bug, just worth knowing for QA/staging; documented in test_credentials.md as @example.com which works fine.

action_items: Consider wrapping the LlmChat.send_message calls in /api/ai/stylist and /api/lookbooks/{id}/recreate to return a graceful 200 with an explanatory message on LLM gateway errors (budget exceeded, timeout, rate limit) instead of HTTPException(500).

If the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget cap is intentionally low ($0.001), consider raising it or surfacing 'AI temporarily unavailable' more clearly to users; testing observed sporadic budget-exceeded failures across the test run.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 835 lines and growing — should be split into modules (auth, items, outfits, ai, lookbooks) before adding more features.

ai_tag_item swallows all LLM errors and returns 'Untagged item' (good), but ai_stylist and recreate_lookbook raise HTTPException(500) on the same class of failure — inconsistent error handling pattern.

Google session endpoint (/api/auth/google/session) is not testable end-to-end in this environment; logic looks correct (checks Emergent OAuth, upserts user, stores session) but cannot be verified by automated test.
All routes correctly enforce auth scoping by user_id (verified by 4 cross-user tests on items list/get/update/delete).
MongoDB _id is properly excluded everywhere via projection {'_id': 0}.
JWT_SECRET has a non-trivial default in .env (good). bcrypt + jwt usage is standard and correct.
seed_data_creation: Two ephemeral test users created per run (test_usera_* and test_userb_* @example.com) with random suffixes — no persistent seed data. Three items created for user_a (one auto-tagged, two with manual tags) and two items created for user_b via camera-roll scan. One outfit created and deleted within the test run; one item deleted at the end. Lookbooks are static curated entries in code.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL) from /app/frontend/.env. Register fresh test users on every run — emails are lowercased server-side, so keep the local-part lowercase in fixtures. .test TLDs are rejected by Pydantic EmailStr — use @example.com. AI endpoints (tag-item, stylist, recreate) typically respond in 2-10s but plan for occasional Emergent LLM budget-exceeded 500s on /ai/stylist and /lookbooks/{id}/recreate; the test_wardrobe_api.py suite is idempotent and safe to rerun. Frontend testing intentionally skipped this pass.
rca_of_issue: On the first test pass, /api/lookbooks/{id}/recreate returned 500. Backend log showed: 'litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.00613725, Max budget: 0.001'. This is the Emergent LLM proxy's per-key cost cap kicking in after multiple GPT-5.2 calls in the suite (tag-item, 1 auto-tag during create_item, stylist, then recreate). On rerun the call succeeded (200). Mitigation: wrap LLM calls in try/except and return graceful 200 with fallback message, matching the pattern already used in ai_tag_item.
